Demons (Doctrine)
DEE-munz
noun (demonology)
Greek daimonion (evil spirit, demon). The fallen angels in the service of Satan; the evil spirits that oppose God, afflict and possess men, and promote idolatry and deception. Distinguished in Scripture from the holy angels by their rebellion and corruption.

📖 Biblical Definition

Greek daimonion (evil spirit, demon); the fallen angels in the service of Satan, the evil spirits that oppose God, afflict and possess men, and promote idolatry and deception. The biblical doctrine of demons. (1) Their identity: demons are the fallen angels (the angels that sinned, 2 Peter 2:4; Jude 1:6; Satan's angels, Matthew 25:41; Revelation 12:9), real personal spiritual beings in rebellion against God. (2) Their activity: demons tempt to sin; afflict with physical and mental torment (the demoniacs of the Gospels); possess men (Mark 5:1-20, the Gerasene demoniac; many Gospel accounts); promote idolatry (1 Corinthians 10:20, the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils, and not to God); spread false doctrine (1 Timothy 4:1, doctrines of devils); and oppose the kingdom of God. (3) Their subjection to Christ: the demons recognize and fear Christ (Mark 1:24, I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God; James 2:19, the devils also believe, and tremble); they are cast out by Christ's authority and the authority He gave His disciples (Matthew 10:1; Luke 10:17-20; Acts 16:18); they are wholly subject to His sovereign power. (4) Their destiny: the demons face certain final judgment (Matthew 25:41, the everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels). The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive biblical doctrine of demons against both the rationalist denial (demons as primitive explanations for disease and mental illness) and the demon-obsessed excess (the hyper-charismatic demon-behind-every-bush spirituality, the elaborate deliverance-ministry systems, the territorial-spirits and generational-curses schemes). Demons are real, personal, fallen-angelic beings, active in opposition to God and His people, but wholly subject to the sovereign authority of Christ; the believer resists them through the means God has appointed (the armor of God, Ephesians 6; sober vigilance, 1 Peter 5:8; submission to God and resistance of the devil, James 4:7) and rests in the certain victory of Christ over the whole demonic host.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Greek daimonion; the fallen angels in the service of Satan; evil spirits that tempt, afflict, possess, and promote idolatry and false doctrine; real personal beings wholly subject to the authority of Christ; destined for certain judgment (Matthew 25:41).

DEMONS (DOCTRINE), n. (demonology; Greek daimonion, evil spirit) The fallen angels in the service of Satan; the evil spirits opposing God. Identity: the fallen angels (2 Peter 2:4; Matthew 25:41; Revelation 12:9). Activity: tempt to sin; afflict and possess (the Gospel demoniacs, Mark 5:1-20); promote idolatry (1 Corinthians 10:20); spread false doctrine (1 Timothy 4:1). Subjection to Christ: recognize and fear Him (Mark 1:24; James 2:19, the devils also believe, and tremble); cast out by His authority (Matthew 10:1; Luke 10:17-20). Destiny: certain final judgment (Matthew 25:41). Held against the rationalist denial and the demon-obsessed hyper-charismatic excess; demons are real but wholly subject to Christ's sovereign authority.

📖 Key Scripture

James 2:19 — "Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble."

Mark 1:24 — "Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God."

1 Corinthians 10:20 — "But I say, that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils, and not to God: and I would not that ye should have fellowship with devils."

Luke 10:17 — "And the seventy returned again with joy, saying, Lord, even the devils are subject unto us through thy name."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Demons are real personal fallen-angelic beings wholly subject to Christ; the corruptions are the rationalist denial (demons as primitive disease-explanations) and the demon-obsessed hyper-charismatic excess (deliverance-ministry systems, territorial spirits, generational curses).

expand to see more

Demons as a doctrine is held against two opposing errors. The rationalist denial treats demons as primitive pre-scientific explanations for disease and mental illness, denying their reality as personal spiritual beings; this contradicts the substantive biblical witness, including the Lord Jesus's own treatment of demons as real personal beings whom He addressed, commanded, and cast out (and the Gospel's careful distinction between demon-possession and ordinary illness, e.g. Matthew 4:24). The demon-obsessed excess (the hyper-charismatic demon-behind-every-bush spirituality; the elaborate deliverance-ministry systems; the territorial-spirits mapping; the generational-curses schemes requiring specific deliverance prayers) goes far beyond the substantive biblical data and produces a fear-driven, demon-focused spirituality that displaces the believer's confidence in Christ's victory. The patriarchal-Reformed reader holds the substantive biblical doctrine within its proper bounds: demons are real, personal, fallen-angelic beings, active in opposition to God and His people; they tempt, afflict, possess (in the biblical sense), promote idolatry, and spread false doctrine; but they are wholly subject to the sovereign authority of Christ (the demons believe and tremble, James 2:19; they are subject to His name, Luke 10:17). The believer resists demons through the appointed means (the armor of God, Ephesians 6:10-18; sober vigilance, 1 Peter 5:8; submission to God and resistance of the devil, James 4:7) and rests in the certain victory of Christ over the whole demonic host — not in fear-driven deliverance systems but in the sufficient, finished, sovereign triumph of Christ at the cross (Colossians 2:15).
